call_points.text: FY27 order inflow target held at ₹8,000 Cr, with management saying it will try to cross it.
Order book ₹14,424 Cr at 30 June 2026; consultancy ₹10,498 Cr, turnkey ₹3,926 Cr.
Middle East new mega projects on hold; Aramco still in initial stages with no major inquiry.
Coal gasification: bidding for feasibility studies after the government's ₹34,000 Cr gap-funding policy.
No provision write-backs expected; guarantee and warranty provisions reverse only after the defect liability period.
RFCL now contributing regularly; a dividend from it is expected this financial year.
No plan to distribute the surplus cash; other investment plans under consideration.
Analyst pressed on consultancy execution rate; management called it cyclical and declined a specific figure.
Asked for the bid pipeline size, management said it was difficult to quantify.
Consultancy revenue growth guided at 15-20% for FY27.
Overall revenue growth expected at minimum 10-15% for FY27.
Consultancy segment margin maintained at 20-25%; LSTK business at 5-7%.
Order book at all-time high of ₹15,109 Cr as on 31 March 2026, up from ₹11,717 Cr a year ago.
Middle East accounts for 10-15% of order book; new awards delayed by a couple of months due to conflict.
Dangote refinery order worth $360 mn and fertilizer order $70 mn; execution over four years.
Company paid interim dividend of ₹2.5 per share (₹140 Cr) and proposed final dividend of ₹2.5 per share.
Middle East conflict has slowed new project awards; management cautious on near-term order inflow.
Associate plant back to full capacity after shutdown; expected to run at 100% this year.

guidance.statement: Order inflow target of ₹8,000 Cr for FY27, with an attempt to exceed it
Total turnover growth of at least 10% to about ₹4,200 Cr
Consultancy turnover of ₹2,300-2,400 Cr, at least 55% of total turnover
Operating margin of 16%, with upside if change orders settle

operating_notes.text: Order book at ₹15,109 Cr as on 31 March 2026, with consultancy order book over ₹10,000 Cr.
Middle East accounts for 10-15% of order book and 30% of overseas business secured.
Dangote refinery order $360 mn and fertilizer order $70 mn, execution over four years.
Order book of ₹14,424 Cr at 30 June 2026 splits into ₹10,498 Cr consultancy and ₹3,926 Cr turnkey.
Business won so far in FY27 is ₹2,750 Cr, of which about ₹1,100 Cr is overseas and about ₹1,500 Cr is domestic LSTK.
Infrastructure contributes around 45% of business income in the current financial year, and the company is setting up a CBG plant with its own money.
